name: context_runtime
description: Identify this RightClick X instance: version, runtime (node/bun/deno/workers/browser), region, graph size and powers, receipt-chain head.

name: context_research
description: Research the environment: what runtime and platform bindings exist, which semantic types the graph produces and consumes, which inputs have no producer yet (gaps), and — given a topic — which public sources worldwide (APIs.guru OpenAPI directory, the official MCP Registry) could add powers. Pass learn:N to pull the top N candidates straight into the graph.

learn.description: Learn the top N candidates immediately.

name: context_learn
description: Discover capabilities from a URL (OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, peer or web page) or an operator-authorised local program (cli:/absolute/path). Reports learned capabilities and graph changes; discovery never grants execution authority.

source.description: URL or cli:/absolute/path to an authorised program.

deep.description: Also probe well-known locations at the origin.

name: context_forget
description: Remove a provider and its capabilities from the live graph.

name: context_inspect
description: Classify any value into the semantic type lattice (url, email, language, place, geo.lat, html, markdown, json, ...).

name: context_actions
description: What can be done with this value right now: capabilities that accept it directly, plus every semantic type it can be turned into through multi-step pipelines.

type.description: Or a semantic type instead of a value.

name: context_explain
description: Get a capability's execution contract: all typed inputs, options and outputs, authority, current restrictions, evidence grade, stored checks and limitations. Default detail: run. Request full for raw synthetic examples, the full card, graph neighbours and run history.

detail.description: run (default) keeps execution constraints and evidence; full adds underlying detail.

name: context_run
description: Run one capability now. Saved goal:<slug> capabilities re-plan against the current environment, heal API changes and repeat their stored result checks and independent witnesses. Returns output, timing, receipt, verification and witness evidence. Optional predicates add checks; they never remove stored checks. A failed call to a learned API re-reads its contract once and retries the same operation if the API moved; an id that re-learning pointed at a different operation remains refused; caller acknowledgement cannot authorise the change. Large outputs: pass view to get a count, field projection or slice instead of the whole payload.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

select.description: Path into the output, e.g. "items", "0.sequence.length", or "isoforms.accession" to map over an array.

fields.description: Project each element onto these paths, e.g. ["accession","sequence.length"].

count.description: Return only the number of elements, keys or characters of the selected value.

offset.description: Start of a slice of the selected array (default 0).

limit.description: Length of a slice of the selected array.

full.description: Return the selected value whole, even when it is over the response budget.

view.description: What to return of the output: a count, a projection or a slice. Without a view, an output over 32000 characters of JSON is withheld whole (never cut) and summarised by size, count and shape. The run record and receipt digest always cover the full output.

name: context_run_status
description: Read a previous run by runId, or list recent runs. Also reports whether the receipt chain is intact. With runId, view counts, projects or slices that run's recorded output without running it again.

limit.description: Length of a slice of the selected array.

name: context_compose
description: Give what you have and the type you want; RightClick X discovers routes across the environment and (with run:true) executes, checks and repairs them. Currency/unit refinements require explicit conversions. Attach witnesses for independent business-outcome checks. publish saves a stable goal:<slug> capability another AI can discover with context_graph and invoke with context_run; its checks survive restart and API changes. A successful multi-step pipeline is also saved for reuse.

have.description: Named inputs, e.g. {"place":"Lisbon","language":"es"} or {"x":{"type":"url","value":"https://..."}}. With publish, {"to":{"value":"EUR","fixed":true}} pins an input inside the published goal instead of making it a parameter of its API.

want.description: Desired semantic type, e.g. text, language, geo.lat, html, hash.

intent.description: Words describing the goal, e.g. 'weather forecast translated'.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

witnesses.description: Independent outcome checks, repeated for every saved invocation. Discover a read-only checker in the environment. Example: [{"capability":"<checker id>","args":{"order_id":{"input":"order_id"},"tax_amount":{"output":""}},"verify":[{"op":"equals","path":"valid","value":true}]}]. input paths read this invocation's have values; output paths read the candidate result (empty string = whole result); value supplies a literal. The checker must be a separate provider and must pass its predicates. Its contract is pinned on save; a changed checker fails closed.

output.description: Path in the candidate output; empty string selects all of it.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

confirm.description: Required to run plans containing destructive capabilities.

publish.description: After a successful run, save this goal as goal:<slug> in the graph AND as /x/<slug> in the synthesized API. Checks and witnesses are retained and re-run on every invocation. Stored predicates make a goal "checked"; an independent witness makes it "verified".

acquire.description: If nothing in the graph can do it: research public directories (APIs.guru, MCP Registry), learn the best candidates and re-plan.

through.description: Anchors: capability ids or search phrases the pipeline must pass through; the planner wires the types between them.

risks.description: Optional constraint: plan only with these risk labels, e.g. ["read"].

require.description: Required information the result must carry, e.g. ["resolution"] or ["gene name"]. Plans are judged by the fields their result declares and by how each join is supported; only an established plan runs, otherwise the outcome says unavailable/unverified and nothing runs. After running, the output is checked for every term.

origins.description: Optional egress policy, e.g. ["https://api.example.com"]: use only capabilities that send data to these origins, now and in every automatic repair. Saved with publish.

select.description: Path into the output, e.g. "items", "0.sequence.length", or "isoforms.accession" to map over an array.

fields.description: Project each element onto these paths, e.g. ["accession","sequence.length"].

limit.description: Length of a slice of the selected array.

name: context_graph
description: Query the live graph. op: stats | types | search (query) | neighbors (id) | paths (from, to) | edges | export | authority. authority audits consequential execution capabilities and operator restrictions; it cannot change policy.

name: context_providers
description: Providers currently contributing capabilities: builtins, platform, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, web, peers, crystallized pipelines.

name: context_watch
description: Follow the graph as it changes: providers learned/forgotten, runs, crystallizations, research. Pass the returned cursor back as since; waitMs long-polls.

waitMs.description: Wait up to this long for new events.
